claims.text: Under sustained loading, nanoscale elastic undulations at multilayer interfaces act as precursors to deformation twinning in high-entropy-alloy multilayers.
Interface undulations and the resulting deformation twinning govern progressive plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy multilayers.
Compositional complexity produces variations in local stacking-fault energy.
Local stacking-fault-energy variations modulate how interface undulations facilitate twin formation and subsequent plastic flow.
The initial high-entropy-alloy multilayers possess inherent compositional variations while retaining a nanoscale layered structure.
Local stacking-fault-energy heterogeneity can be deliberately altered through compositional tuning while preserving the multilayer architecture.
The relevant elastic undulations have a characteristic wavelength of approximately 1–2 nm.
The nanoscale elastic undulations occur at multilayer interfaces and evolve into deformation twins.
Sustained loading produces geometrical nonlinearity at multilayer interfaces, leading to elastic undulations.
Regions with lower local stacking-fault energy more readily convert elastic undulations into deformation twins.
Undulation-triggered twinning causes a transition from elastic to plastic deformation.
Deformation twinning redistributes stress and accommodates progressive plastic strain during creep.
Multilayers with greater local stacking-fault-energy heterogeneity will exhibit earlier onset and greater density of elastic undulations and deformation twins.
Greater stacking-fault-energy heterogeneity will accelerate creep strain relative to the starting baseline.
Multilayers with more uniform stacking-fault energy will show delayed or reduced twin formation under otherwise identical loading.
The proposed mechanism dominates only while nanoscale multilayer architecture is retained.
The proposed mechanism dominates only at temperatures where displacive deformation prevails over diffusion-mediated deformation.
Extreme temperatures or layer thicknesses may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
A lack of statistically significant differences in undulation onset, twin formation, and creep strain rate between heterogeneous-SFE and uniform-SFE samples would falsify the hypothesis.
